rationale: Repeatability of the methodology is evidence that Kindervag provides actionable strategy.
The protect surface (shifting controls from perimeter to asset) is the architectural mechanism that eliminates implicit trust.
Nation-state incidents (SolarWinds, Exchange) are the empirical evidence that perimeter-based security is structurally broken.
Historical origin in Morris Worm and academic thesis refutes the claim that ZT is vendor marketing.
NIST's articulation that ZT adoption is an incremental journey supports the 'journey not destination' framing.
NIST's definition of ZT as an architectural paradigm (not a product) independently supports the strategy-not-product claim.
The operational mechanism (assume breach, continuous auth) is what enables the design goal (prevent breaches, limit lateral movement).
The semantic clarification that ZT means 'zero implicit trust' aligns directly with NIST's operational definition of eliminating implicit trust.
The three core principles (secure all resources, least privilege, inspect/log all traffic) are the universal operational instantiation of assume-breach/continuous-auth.
The physical security analogy (layered zones, no implicit trust) directly illustrates the protect surface concept.
Uncertainty minimization reframes assume-breach/continuous-auth in more precise, measurable terms.
Adds the DoD-vs-NIST comparison dimension to the observation that NIST's tenets are architectural.
Adds the nuance that NIST's architectural tenets are explicitly aspirational, not mandatory requirements.
'Integrated security platform' is a specific, elaborated articulation of the general claim that ZT is a strategy.
Explains the mechanism by which ZT becomes an integrated platform: amplifying and integrating existing concepts (least privilege, RBAC).
Clarifies what is transformative about the three core principles: they aren't just repackaging but amplification into a holistic automated platform.
